# `silk/bench/harness`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The harness of a Silk program whose benchmarks a benchmark task drives: it answers the
driven protocol and times each run.

## When to use
Use a [`Harness`](#Harness) in a program that holds several pieces of work to time, when the samples
of two implementations should be taken in turns from processes that stay alive. Declare the
program in a suite with `silk.bench.suite.Implementation.driven`. A program that does one
piece of work from start to exit needs no harness: a command suite times it as a process.

## Details
A program gives the harness the names of its benchmarks and then loops on
[`Harness.next`](#Harness.impl.next). Each time it returns `true`, the program runs the body of
[`Harness.name`](#Harness.impl.name) exactly [`Harness.iterations`](#Harness.impl.iterations) times. The harness times from the return of
`next` to the next call, and answers with a result line in `ns/op`.

Started by a benchmark task, the harness follows the commands of the task, which decides
how many iterations a sample takes and takes the samples of the implementations in turns.
The dialogue is the one `silk.bench.transport` describes, over the `Transport` service.

Started by hand, the same program is a benchmark of its own: for each name the harness
finds an iteration count that takes about 50 ms, or what [`Harness.sample`](#Harness.impl.sample) sets, then
takes 10 samples, and prints them as result lines, which a suite reads with `Implementation.resultLines` and tools such as
`benchstat` read too.

[`Harness.reset`](#Harness.impl.reset) starts the timing again after setup that should not count, and
[`Harness.stop`](#Harness.impl.stop) and [`Harness.start`](#Harness.impl.start) leave a stretch out. [`Harness.check`](#Harness.impl.check) reports what
the run computed, so the task can tell when two implementations did different work,
[`Harness.keep`](#Harness.impl.keep) stops the compiler from removing or precomputing the work, and
[`Harness.value`](#Harness.impl.value) adds a value in another unit to the result line.

## Gotchas
A body whose result is never used may be removed by the compiler, and a body that computes
the same value every time may be run once. Give the result of each iteration, and its
input, to [`Harness.keep`](#Harness.impl.keep).

## Implementation `Harness`

```silk
impl Harness
```

<a id="Harness.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect fn make(names: &[string], driven: bool) -> Harness
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns a harness for the benchmarks `names`. With `driven`, it follows the commands that
arrive over the `Transport`; without, it runs every benchmark itself and sends the result
lines.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the names.

<a id="Harness.impl.open"></a>

### Associated function `open`

```silk
pub effect fn open(names: &[string]) -> Harness
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator | &mut HostInput
```

Returns a harness for the benchmarks `names` that is driven when a benchmark task started
the program, which the task says with the environment variable `BENCH_DRIVE`.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the names.

<a id="Harness.impl.next"></a>

### Method `next`

```silk
pub effect fn next(self: &mut Self) -> bool
    ! TransportError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Transport | &mut Allocator | &mut MonotonicClock
```

Finishes the run in progress, if there is one, and returns whether there is another run
to do. After `true`, run the body of [`Harness.name`](#Harness.impl.name) [`Harness.iterations`](#Harness.impl.iterations) times and
call `next` again.

#### Errors
- `TransportError` if a line cannot be carried.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply a line.

<a id="Harness.impl.sample"></a>

### Method `sample`

```silk
pub fn sample(self: &mut Self, milliseconds: u64) -> ()
```

Sets how long one sample should take when nobody drives the harness, in milliseconds. A
driven harness takes the iteration counts of its task and ignores this.

Returns the name of the benchmark to run, as it was given to the harness.

<a id="Harness.impl.failed"></a>

### Method `failed`


Says that the run failed, with `text` as the reason on one line. The harness answers with
an `error:` line and no result line.

### Method `stop`

```silk

    ? &mut MonotonicClock
```

Stops the timing, until [`Harness.start`](#Harness.impl.start). Stopping twice changes nothing.

<a id="Harness.impl.start"></a>

### Method `start`

```silk
pub effect fn start(self: &mut Self) -> ()
    ? &mut MonotonicClock
```

Starts the timing again after [`Harness.stop`](#Harness.impl.stop). Starting twice changes nothing.

<a id="Harness.impl.check"></a>

### Method `check`

```silk
pub effect fn check(self: &mut Self, text: string) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Reports `text` as what the run computed, such as a checksum. A benchmark task does not
compare implementations whose checks differ.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.


Reports `number` as what the run computed. See [`Harness.check`](#Harness.impl.check).

<a id="Harness.impl.value"></a>

### Method `value`

```silk
pub effect fn value(self: &mut Self, unit: string, amount: f64) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds `amount` in `unit` to the result line of the run, such as 1024 `B/op`. A unit holds
no space.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.

<a id="Harness.impl.keep"></a>

### Associated function `keep`

```silk
pub fn keep<T>(value: &T) -> ()
```

Makes the compiler treat `value` as read and written, so it can neither remove the work
that computed it nor assume what it holds. Give it the result of each iteration, and an
input the compiler could otherwise compute with.

#### Gotchas
On a target without inline assembly, which is every target but Linux on x86_64 and
aarch64 and macOS on aarch64, the value is only made to live in memory, which stops less.

<a id="Harness.impl.grown"></a>

### Associated function `grown`

```silk
pub fn grown(iterations: u64, elapsed: u64, target: u64) -> u64
```

Returns the iteration count to try after `iterations` took `elapsed` nanoseconds, when a
sample should take `target`: enough to reach the target with a fifth to spare, at least
twice and at most a hundred times as many.
